variant_desc: 10M bytes scanned: per-byte noinline read helper vs inlined loop
source_citation: https://fgiesen.wordpress.com/2016/01/02/end-of-buffer-checks-in-decompressors/ — Fabian Giesen 2016 on abstraction-induced redundancy in stream consumers.
novelty_rationale: Tests whether the LLM knows to remove tiny per-byte wrapper abstractions whose noinline boundary prevents the compiler from dissolving the per-call bounds check AND prevents auto-vectorization of the byte-sum reduction. CSE cannot hoist a check whose condition (cursor) changes every call; only API restructuring (removing the wrapper) helps. Empirical speedup includes both per-call overhead removal (~5-10×) and SIMD reduction unlock (~16×), composing to ~100×. This is the HR-style framing of the same end-of-buffer pattern as HO-CF-4 — distinct framing: HR emphasizes the abstraction cost, CF emphasizes the branchless refill design.
